pages.name: About
pages.seoDescription: A ten-seat omakase counter behind the old fish market — bought small and daily, rice seasoned by hand, wasabi grated to order, served at the pace it’s meant to be eaten.

children.class: mx-auto flex w-full max-w-3xl flex-col gap-6

children: Nori is a ten-seat sushi counter in a quiet room behind the old fish market. There is no long menu and no à-la-carte rush — you sit at the bar, the chef reads the day’s fish, and the meal comes to you a piece at a time, in the order it’s meant to be eaten.

We buy small and buy daily, from a handful of suppliers we’ve worked with for years. The rice is seasoned by hand and served at body temperature; the wasabi is grated to order; the nori is kept dry until the moment it’s rolled. Little of that is visible on a plate — all of it is the point.

The room is small on purpose, and the pace is deliberate. Book ahead — both seatings fill early at the weekend — and come a little hungry. A stool at the end of the bar is kept for walk-ins whenever one opens.
